sources.title: Elliptic curve discrete logarithms and the index calculus
sources.citation: Joseph H. Silverman and Joe Suzuki, ASIACRYPT 1998, LNCS 1514, Springer, 1998, pp. 110-125.
sources.notes: Paywalled; only the chapter landing text and the Huang-Kueh-Tan abstract were read (2026-11-02). Conclusion as summarized there: the natural generalization of index calculus to E is less efficient than brute force, supported by theoretical and numerical evidence. No theorem numbers are recorded.

sources.title: Lifting elliptic curves and solving the elliptic curve discrete logarithm problem
sources.citation: Ming-Deh A. Huang, Ka Lam Kueh and Ki-Seng Tan, ANTS-IV, LNCS 1838, Springer, 2000, pp. 377-384.
sources.notes: Abstract only (via search indexes, 2026-11-02): the fundamental obstruction is the need to lift an asymptotically increasing number of random points to bounded-height rational points; a method meeting this requirement yields a method to construct elliptic curves over Q of arbitrarily large rank. Theorem numbering not seen.

nodes.label: ECDLP lifting problem (Silverman)
nodes.statement: Given E/F_p and S, T in E(F_p), find a ring R in a field K, an ideal p of R with R/p = F_p, a curve E^/K reducing to E mod p, and points S^, T^ in E^(K) reducing to S, T. Variants: K local (Q_p) or global (Q, number field); lifted points torsion or nontorsion.
nodes.scope: Framework for the four lifting faces (local/global x torsion/nontorsion). Xedni is the global-nontorsion 'easy lifting' face; Smart's anomalous attack is a local-nontorsion lift that works only because l = p.
source_locations: Silverman 2007 slides 4-5 ('The Elliptic Curve Lifting Problem', 'The Four Faces')

nodes.label: Index calculus on a lift E~(Q)
nodes.statement: Lift E/F_p to E~/Q, take the factor base to be the points of small canonical height in E~(Q), lift random [a]P+[b]Q to E~(Q) and decompose them over the factor base by descent; reduce the relations mod p.
nodes.scope: The direct analogue of finite-field index calculus (lift to Z, factor over small primes). Distinct from summation-polynomial index calculus and from xedni, which lifts a fixed small number of points simultaneously.

nodes.label: Miller's height argument against lifted index calculus
nodes.statement: E~(Q) has very few points of small height, so random points [a]P+[b]Q from the exponentially large E(F_p) would have to lift to points of exponentially large height; in addition the lifting itself is a nonlinear Diophantine problem over Z.
nodes.scope: Brief heuristic in the paper that proposed elliptic-curve cryptography; Galbraith and later authors call it a heuristic argument, not a theorem.
assumptions: Points of E~(Q) of height <= B are sparse (rank and height-counting behaviour of E~)
Random lifts behave like generic points of E~(Q)
non_implications: Does not rule out lifts that avoid small-height factor bases (e.g. xedni's simultaneous lifts)
Not a lower bound for any algorithm

nodes.label: Silverman-Suzuki: lifted index calculus slower than brute force
nodes.statement: A detailed analysis of the natural generalization of index calculus to elliptic curves concludes that it is less efficient than brute-force search, supporting Miller's view with theoretical and numerical evidence.
nodes.scope: Analysis of the lift-and-decompose approach of DEF-XT-LIFTED-INDEX-CALCULUS; the abstract-level summaries do not state an unconditional theorem.
assumptions: Height/rank heuristics for the lifted curves
Numerical evidence on small examples
source_locations: Silverman-Suzuki 1998, LNCS 1514 pp. 110-125 (whole paper; theorem numbers not seen)

nodes.label: Huang-Kueh-Tan: bounded-height lifting implies arbitrarily large rank
nodes.statement: Any method that lifts an asymptotically increasing number of random points of E(F_p) to rational points of bounded height on curves over Q (as lifted index calculus requires) yields a method for constructing elliptic curves over Q of arbitrarily large rank.
nodes.scope: Applies to lifting schemes whose number of lifted points grows; a fixed-size simultaneous lift (classic xedni, at most 9 points) is not covered.
assumptions: The lifting scheme lifts a growing number of random points with bounded height
source_locations: Huang-Kueh-Tan 2000, main theorem as stated in the abstract (LNCS 1838 pp. 377-384)
non_implications: Does not by itself refute lifting: unbounded rank over Q is not disproved
Does not cover fixed-r simultaneous lifts

nodes.label: PPVW heuristic: ranks of E/Q are bounded (finitely many > 21)
nodes.statement: Modeling ranks and Shafarevich-Tate groups by random alternating matrices, the model proves (Theorem 1.1.1) that with probability 1 all but finitely many E have model rank <= 21 and #{E: ht E <= H, rank >= r} = H^((21-r)/24+o(1)) for 1 <= r <= 20; the heuristic is that actual ranks behave like the model.
nodes.scope: The theorem is about the random model; the transfer to rk E(Q) is a heuristic, and special families may deviate (Remark 1.1.2).
assumptions: Actual ranks and Sha follow the random alternating-matrix model
non_implications: Not a theorem about rk E(Q)
Says nothing about curves over number fields of growing degree

nodes.label: Bounded rank would rule out growing-factor-base lifting
nodes.statement: If ranks of elliptic curves over Q are bounded (as the PPVW heuristic predicts), then by Huang-Kueh-Tan no method can lift an asymptotically increasing number of random points to bounded height on curves over Q, so lifted index calculus over Q with a growing factor base cannot work.
nodes.scope: Composition of HKT's theorem with the boundedness heuristic, made in this corpus; neither paper states it in this form.
assumptions: Huang-Kueh-Tan theorem as stated in their abstract
Ranks over Q are bounded (heuristic)
non_implications: Says nothing about lifts to number fields of growing degree

nodes.label: Cheng-Huang: ECDLP reduces to three partial lifting problems
nodes.statement: ECDLP reduces to three partial lifting problems, under heuristic conjectures about the ranks of elliptic curves.
nodes.scope: Refines the HKT lifting obstacle into partial lifting subproblems; no algorithm for the partial lifting problems is given.
assumptions: Heuristic rank conjectures stated in the paper

nodes.label: Local nontorsion lifts lose the relation T = mS
nodes.statement: Hensel lifting of S and T to E^(Q_p) has p choices at each step; once S_2 is chosen only one of p lifts of T preserves T_2 = m S_2, and no method is known to make consistent choices without knowing m. If a consistent lift were available, log_F(N T^)/log_F(N S^) with N = #E(F_p) would give m.
nodes.scope: Counting fact proved; the absence of a consistent-choice method is an open negative, not a theorem.
assumptions: l != p for the subgroup order (otherwise Smart's attack applies)
non_implications: Does not prove that consistent lifting is hard

nodes.label: Local torsion lifts preserve the relation but land in the formal-group kernel
nodes.statement: A point of order n != p has a unique lift of order n in E(Q_p), so T^ = m S^ holds for torsion lifts; but multiplying by n to enter the formal group gives O = mO, and no efficient ECDLP method in E(Q_p) is known without the formal group.
nodes.scope: Uniqueness of the torsion lift is proved; 'no method known' is an open negative.
assumptions: n coprime to p

nodes.label: Only l = p torsion leaks through E(Z/p^2)
nodes.statement: E(Z/p^2) is an extension of E(F_p) by the formal-group layer, isomorphic to F_p^+; l-torsion with l != p lifts isomorphically, so the only homomorphic leak to an additive group is for l = p (the anomalous case). Published generalisations of Smart (Belding; Abdullah-Mahalanobis-Mallick) all require l = p.
nodes.scope: Repository synthesis of a standard structural argument; consistent with OBS-XT-LOCAL-TORSION-LIFT.
assumptions: Good reduction at p

nodes.label: Global torsion lifts: torsion too small over Q, fields too large otherwise
nodes.statement: Lifting S, T to torsion points of E^(Q) would preserve T^ = mS^ and make m easy, but #E^(Q)_tors <= 16 (Mazur); over a number field K containing a point of order n, generally [K:Q] >= c #GL_2(Z/nZ) ~ c n^4 (Serre), so the field is too large to compute in.
nodes.scope: Mazur and Serre are quoted on the slides without proof; the Serre bound is stated as holding 'generally' (non-CM, open-image situations).
assumptions: Serre open-image hypotheses for the degree bound

nodes.label: Petsche: torsion bound polynomial in degree and Szpiro ratio
nodes.statement: For E/k with [k:Q] = d and Szpiro ratio sigma, |E(k)_tors| <= c1 d sigma^2 log(c2 d sigma^2) with c1 = 134861, c2 = 104613.
nodes.scope: Explicit refinement of Hindry-Silverman's exponential bound; uniform in k only if Szpiro's conjecture bounds sigma.

nodes.label: Masser: dependent specializations have density zero
nodes.statement: For a parameterized family E_U with parameterized points Q_{1,U},...,Q_{r,U} that are generically independent, the set of u in Q^n at which the specialized points are dependent in E_u(Q) is small (density 0).
nodes.scope: Quoted on the Silverman slides without a precise reference or proof.
assumptions: Generic independence over the function field

nodes.label: Easy-lift (xedni) points are dependent with probability below 1/p
nodes.statement: Viewing the curve coefficients as parameters, Masser's theorem suggests that the probability that simultaneously lifted points (up to 9 through a cubic) are linearly dependent is less than 1/p; choosing curves to 'encourage' small rank (BSD-guided, Mestre-Nagao-style) still leaves the lifted points independent in practice.
nodes.scope: Silverman's own summary of why the easy lifting method (xedni) fails; independent of, and consistent with, JKSST's C0/p conditional bound.
assumptions: Density-zero statement transfers to a per-instance probability bound
Rank-lowering curve selection does not correlate with dependence of the chosen points

nodes.label: Hard lifting: the lift of T has canonical height m^2 h(S)
nodes.statement: If E^ and S^ are lifted and T^ = m S^ exists, then h(T^) = m^2 h(S^); with m = Theta(p) writing T^ takes Theta(p^2 h(S^)) bits, and no method is known to find T^ (or describe it implicitly) without m.
nodes.scope: Quadraticity of the canonical height is a theorem; the 'no implicit description' part is open.
assumptions: rank E^(Q) = 1 or T^ known to exist
nodes.formula: h(T^) = m^2 h(S^); size(T^) = O(p^2) bits for m ~ p
non_implications: Quadraticity alone gives no Lang-type lower bound constant (scaled-lattice countermodel in the JKSST Lean audit)

nodes.label: Lang's canonical-height conjecture
nodes.statement: For a number field k there is c(k) > 0 with h(P) >= c(k) log|N_{k/Q}(Delta_{E/k})| for every elliptic curve E/k and every non-torsion P in E(k).
nodes.scope: Open in general; known conditionally on Szpiro's conjecture (Hindry-Silverman) and with explicit Szpiro-ratio-dependent constants (Petsche). It is one of the bridge hypotheses of the JKSST xedni obstruction.

cited_by.note: Compares lifted-point Lang ratios (~1/6) with a Hindry-Silverman-type constant of order 1e-15.

nodes.label: Szpiro's conjecture (Szpiro ratio bounded, 6 the largest limit point)
nodes.statement: The set of Szpiro ratios sigma = log|N(Delta_{E/k})| / log|N(f_{E/k})| of elliptic curves over k is bounded, with 6 its largest limit point.
nodes.scope: Open over number fields (follows from ABC); the function-field analogue is known (sigma <= 6).
source_locations: Petsche 2006, Section 1 (definition (1) and the conjecture following Theorem 1)

nodes.label: Hindry-Silverman: Szpiro implies Lang
nodes.statement: Lang's height conjecture holds with a constant depending (exponentially) on [k:Q] and the Szpiro ratio; in particular Szpiro's conjecture implies Lang's conjecture.
nodes.scope: Reported by Petsche; the original constants were not read.
assumptions: Bounded Szpiro ratio to get a uniform constant
source_locations: Hindry-Silverman 1988 (as reported in Petsche 2006, Section 1, discussion after Theorem 2)

nodes.label: Petsche: explicit Lang-type height lower bound in d and sigma
nodes.statement: For E/k with [k:Q] = d, minimal discriminant Delta and Szpiro ratio sigma, every non-torsion P in E(k) has h(P) >= c(d,sigma) log|N_{k/Q}(Delta)| with c(d,sigma) = 1/(10^15 d^3 sigma^6 log^2(c2 d sigma^2)), c2 = 104613.
nodes.scope: Unconditional but non-uniform: the constant degrades polynomially with sigma. A family of lifts with bounded Szpiro ratio inherits an explicit Lang constant without assuming Lang.
nodes.formula: h(P) >= log|N(Delta)| / (1e15 d^3 sigma^6 log^2(104613 d sigma^2))
non_implications: Does not bound sigma for the curves an xedni-type lift produces

nodes.label: Semaev/Rueck anomalous attack via logarithmic differentials
nodes.statement: For P in E(F_p) of order p and f_P with div(f_P) = p(P) - p(O), P -> df_P/f_P is a well-defined homomorphism E(F_p)[p] -> Omega_{F_p}(E) (Lemma 26.4.3); writing f_P = t^-p + f_1 t^-(p-1) + ..., df_P/f_P = (f_1 + ...)dt (Lemma 26.4.5), so Q = [a]P gives coefficient a f_1 and the DLP in E(F_p)[p] is solved by a Miller-style power-series computation.
nodes.scope: Anomalous (trace-one) prime-field curves, or more generally the p-torsion in characteristic p; the differential view of the attack that Smart and Satoh-Araki give p-adically.
assumptions: #E(F_p) divisible by p (point of order p)
Power-series expansion at a uniformizer is computable
source_locations: Galbraith 2018 Lemma 26.4.3 and Lemma 26.4.5, Section 26.4.1, pp. 584-585

nodes.label: Satoh-Araki Fermat-quotient anomalous attack
nodes.statement: Polynomial-time discrete logarithm algorithm for anomalous elliptic curves over F_p via Fermat quotients / p-adic lifting, found independently of Smart's and Semaev's formulations.
nodes.scope: Anomalous curves only.
assumptions: #E(F_p) = p

nodes.label: Rueck: p-torsion DLP in Jacobians of curves in characteristic p
nodes.statement: Generalises Semaev's anomalous method to the p-part of the divisor class group of curves of any genus over fields of characteristic p, via an 'additive version of the Tate-Lichtenbaum pairing' that computes the needed coefficient directly; the DLP there is efficiently solvable.
nodes.scope: p-torsion in characteristic p only; complexity statement not transcribed here.
assumptions: Subgroup order divisible by the characteristic
source_locations: Rueck 1999, Math. Comp. 68, pp. 805-806 (main theorem); Galbraith 2018 Section 26.4.1, p. 585

nodes.label: Balasubramanian-Koblitz: E[r] lies in E(F_{q^k}) iff r | q^k - 1
nodes.statement: Let r be a prime dividing #E(F_q) with r not dividing q - 1 and gcd(r,q) = 1. Then E[r] is contained in E(F_{q^k}) if and only if r divides q^k - 1.
nodes.scope: So for r not dividing q-1 the Weil-pairing MOV attack can work in E(F_{q^k}) with k the embedding degree; the case r | q-1 is excluded.
assumptions: r prime, r | #E(F_q)
r does not divide q-1
gcd(r,q) = 1
source_locations: Galbraith 2018 Theorem 26.4.1, p. 584 (proof deferred to BK 1998)

nodes.label: Balasubramanian-Koblitz: small embedding degree is improbable
nodes.statement: For a random prime p in [M/2, M] and a random curve over F_p with a prime number l of points, the probability that l | p^k - 1 for some k <= (log p)^2 is bounded by an effectively computable constant times a factor of order (log M)^9 (log log M)^2 / M.
nodes.scope: Counts curves of prime order; makes the MOV/Frey-Rueck threat negligible for randomly chosen curves. The exact printed form of the bound was not checked against the primary text.
assumptions: Curve and prime chosen at random as in the theorem
Prime group order
nodes.formula: Pr[k <= (log p)^2] <= C (log M)^9 (log log M)^2 / M (transcription unverified)
non_implications: Says nothing about deliberately constructed or special-family curves
Does not price the target-field DLP

nodes.label: ECC2K-130 embedding degree exceeds 10^7
nodes.statement: Exhaustion finds no embedding degree k <= 10^7 for the ECC2K-130 subgroup order r over F_{2^131}, so the MOV/Frey-Rueck target field exceeds 1.31e9 bits.
nodes.scope: Repository exhaustion bound on ord_r(2^131); consistent with BK's prediction that ordinary curves have k of size comparable to r.
assumptions: Correct subgroup order r

nodes.label: Luca-Shparlinski: about z^(1/2+o(1)) MNT curves with CM discriminant <= z
nodes.statement: Heuristic arguments suggest there are only about z^(1/2+o(1)) MNT (low embedding degree, prime order) elliptic curves with complex multiplication discriminant up to z.
nodes.scope: Ordinary low-embedding-degree constructions; supports that low-k ordinary curves are rare and must be built deliberately.
assumptions: Heuristic distribution of the relevant norm-equation solutions

nodes.label: Distortion map
nodes.statement: For E/F_q, a prime r | #E(F_q), a nondegenerate bilinear pairing e on E[r] and P in E(F_q)[r], a distortion map is an endomorphism psi with e(P, psi(P)) != 1.
nodes.scope: Lets a pairing be nondegenerate on a single cyclic subgroup, which is what makes DDH easy on supersingular curves.

nodes.label: Verheul: distortion maps exist on supersingular curves
nodes.statement: If E is supersingular then for any point P in E(F_{q^k}) - {O} a distortion map exists; in particular for P in E(F_q)[r] with k > 1 there is an endomorphism psi (not defined over F_q) with t_r(P, psi(P)) != 1.
nodes.scope: Supersingular curves; the 'Type 1' symmetric-pairing setting.
assumptions: E supersingular
source_locations: Verheul 2004, Thm. 5 (as cited in Galbraith 2018 Section 26.6.1, p. 588)

nodes.label: The trace map distorts some points but not the G1/G2 eigenspaces
nodes.statement: With k = k(q,r) > 1 and Tr(P) = sum over Gal(F_{q^k}/F_q) of sigma(P): Tr(P) is in E(F_q); if P in E[r], P not in E(F_q) and Tr(P) != O then {P, Tr(P)} generates E[r] and Tr is a distortion map for e_r and P; but Tr(Q) = [k]Q on ker(pi_q - 1) and Tr(Q) = O on ker(pi_q - q), so Tr is not a distortion map for the pairing groups G1, G2.
nodes.scope: Exercise-level statements (no printed proof); they explain why ordinary-curve (Type 3) settings lack an efficient homomorphism between G2 and G1 via the trace.
assumptions: r prime

nodes.label: Galbraith-Paterson-Smart pairing types
nodes.statement: Type 1: G1 = G2 (symmetric, supersingular with distortion map); Type 2: G1 != G2 with an efficiently computable homomorphism psi: G2 -> G1; Type 3: G1 != G2 with no efficiently computable homomorphism known in either direction.
nodes.scope: Classification of how the source groups of a pairing relate; determines which DLP/CDH/DDH problems a pairing exposes on each side.
source_locations: Galbraith-Paterson-Smart 2008, Section 2-3 (types); Galbraith 2018 Definition 22.2.14 (pairing groups) and the following remark on psi: G2 -> G1, Section 22.2.3

nodes.label: Rigorous L(1/2) discrete logarithms (Pomerance; F_p index calculus)
nodes.statement: Index calculus in F_p^* with random multipliers from the complementary subgroup and Lanczos/Wiedemann linear algebra solves the DLP in O(L_p(1/2, 2+o(1))) bit operations without heuristics; Pomerance (1987) proved L_{p^n}(1/2) for fields of fixed characteristic.
nodes.scope: The best proved bounds before the quasi-polynomial results for fixed characteristic; for large and medium characteristic no proved L(1/3) algorithm is recorded in the sources read.
assumptions: r^2 does not divide p-1 for the simple version (Exercise 15.5.8 removes it)

nodes.label: Classical NFS smoothness heuristic
nodes.statement: The norms N_f, N_g of the sieved polynomials are B-smooth with the same probability as arbitrary positive integers of the same size (Dickman rho), Prob(x^(1+o(1)), y) = Prob(x,y)^(1+o(1)); together with relation-matrix rank and descent heuristics this underlies every L(1/3) NFS/TNFS/exTNFS complexity.
nodes.scope: All NFS-family L(1/3, c) complexities and all key-size estimations derived from them rest on it; no NFS DLP complexity is proved.
assumptions: Norms behave like random integers of the same size
Relations are sufficiently independent
Individual-log descent succeeds
source_locations: Kim-Barbulescu 2016, Section 3 ('We make the usual heuristic ...') and Thm. 1 ('under the classical NFS heuristics')

nodes.label: NFS/SNFS/FFS L(1/3) discrete logarithms
nodes.statement: Heuristically, NFS solves the DLP in F_p^* in L_p(1/3, (64/9)^(1/3)+o(1)); special NFS for special p in L_p(1/3, (32/9)^(1/3)+o(1)); the special function field sieve in F_{p^n} in L(1/3, (32/9)^(1/3)+o(1)) for p <= n^o(sqrt n); Joux-Lercier/JLSV give heuristic L_q(1/3, c) for all finite fields.
nodes.scope: Heuristic complexities; the o(1) term and constant-factor terms decide concrete sizes.
assumptions: Classical NFS heuristics

cited_by.note: Prices DLP in F_(q^k) by L[1/3, c] with c = (32/9)^(1/3), o(1) dropped, called an attacker-favourable lower bound.

nodes.label: Coppersmith's algorithm for F_{2^n}
nodes.statement: Coppersmith's algorithm solves the DLP in F_{2^n}^* in L_q(1/3, (32/9)^(1/3)+o(1)) bit operations as n -> infinity (stated as a conjecture).
nodes.scope: Historic small-characteristic baseline used to size early supersingular pairing parameters; superseded by the 2013-2014 L(1/4) and quasi-polynomial algorithms.
assumptions: Smoothness heuristics for polynomials of the sizes arising

nodes.label: Kim-Barbulescu exTNFS: medium-prime L(1/3, (48/9)^(1/3))
nodes.statement: Under the classical NFS heuristics, for Q = p^n with n = eta*kappa, gcd(eta,kappa) = 1 and p = L_Q(l_p, c_p), 1/3 < l_p (< 2/3 or l_p = 2/3 with c_p < 12^(1/3)): exTNFS-JLSV2 and exTNFS-GJL reach L_Q(1/3,(64/9)^(1/3)); exTNFS-Conj (conjugation polynomial selection, kappa = 12^(-1/3)(log Q/log log Q)^(1/3)) reaches L_Q(1/3,(48/9)^(1/3)); SexTNFS for special p reaches L_Q(1/3,(32/9)^(1/3)); multiple-field variants reach about L_Q(1/3,1.71).
nodes.scope: Medium-prime fields with composite small n, including the n = 6 and n = 12 target fields of BN/BLS12 pairings; 'Conj' names the conjugation method, not a conjecture.
assumptions: Classical NFS heuristics
Polynomial-selection conditions of the table in Theorem 1
source_locations: Kim-Barbulescu 2016, Theorem 1 and its table; Section 3 derivations; Section 6 key-size discussion

nodes.label: Barbulescu-Duquesne: arguments that c cannot go below 32
nodes.statement: Writing NFS variants as L_Q[c] = L_Q(1/3, (c/9)^(1/3)), the constants have descended 64 -> 48 -> 32 (Joux-Pierrot, BGGM, BGK TNFS, Kim-Barbulescu exTNFS); BD give arguments (their Appendix B) that one cannot go below c = 32.
nodes.scope: Arguments, not a lower-bound theorem; restricted to the NFS family as currently structured. Small-characteristic fields are outside it (quasi-polynomial algorithms).
assumptions: NFS-family algorithm structure (two number-field sides, smoothness of norms)
source_locations: Barbulescu-Duquesne 2019, Introduction ('o(1)-less estimation' paragraph) and Appendix B (not present in the HAL text read)
non_implications: Is not a lower bound on finite-field DLP cost
Does not apply to small or fixed characteristic

nodes.label: BD: the 3072-bit BN curve offers about 100 bits, not 128
nodes.statement: For the popular BN curve u = -(2^62 + 2^55 + 1) with 3072-bit F_{p^12}, SexTNFS with kappa = 2, eta = 6, h = t^6 - t^3 - t - 1, log2 A = 7.36, log2 B = 57 gives sieving 2^98.65 (c_sieve ~ 1) plus linear algebra 2^98.73 after a log2 B filtering reduction, total about 2^99.69 operations: the curve 'ensures no more than the 100-bits security level'.
nodes.scope: o(1)-less concrete estimate under Dickman smoothness with Monte Carlo norm sizes; operations counted as additions mod p / clock cycles.
assumptions: Classical NFS heuristics
c_sieve ~ 1 and linear algebra cost 2^5 N^2 calibrated on records
Filtering reduces the matrix by a factor ~ log2 B (heuristic)

nodes.label: Claim: BN curves with a 3072-bit F_{p^12} reach 128-bit security
nodes.statement: BN curves with a 256-bit p and 3072-bit target F_{p^12} match the 128-bit security level (per pre-2015 NIST-style key-size tables used for the target field).
nodes.scope: Pre-TNFS sizing claim. Refuted within the shared heuristic NFS cost model, by an explicit SexTNFS parameterization costing ~2^99.7; not refuted by a completed computation.
assumptions: Target-field DLP priced with classical NFS constants
source_locations: Barbulescu-Duquesne 2019, Section 2.1 (BN curves 'supposed to match the 128-bit security level') and Section 5.2

nodes.label: BD updated pairing key sizes
nodes.statement: For 2^128 target-field DLP cost: BN log2(p^k) = 5534, BLS12 5530, KSS16 ~ 4400, KSS18 ~ 4300 (in the KSS cases the curve side is weaker); 192 bits: KSS18 12200, BLS24 13300; 256 bits: KSS18 26900, BLS24 24700; 128-bit parameter sizes log2 u = 114 (BN), 77 (BLS12), 34 (KSS16), 44 (KSS18).
nodes.scope: Attacker-favourable choices of polynomials and automorphisms; o(1)-less model. Upper-bound style estimates for the attacker's cost, not lower bounds.
assumptions: Classical NFS heuristics
Best polynomials available to the attacker
Calibration constants from records

nodes.label: MSS 2016 key-size method (norm upper bounds, B^2 linear algebra)
nodes.statement: Menezes-Sarkar-Singh survey the 2014-2016 NFS advances for F_{p^n} with small n > 1 and estimate their impact on pairing key lengths using mathematical upper bounds on norm sizes and a linear-algebra cost of about B^2.
nodes.scope: Barbulescu-Duquesne argue the method gives an upper bound on attack complexity (useful to show feasibility) but not a security estimate, which would need a lower bound; it ignores filtering and uses B instead of the factor-base size 2B/log B.
assumptions: Classical NFS heuristics
Norm upper bounds as proxy for typical norms
source_locations: Menezes-Sarkar-Singh 2016, Sections 6.3 and Table 3 (as cited by Barbulescu-Duquesne 2019, Section 4.3)

nodes.label: No lower bound for target-field DLP cost exists
nodes.statement: Pairing key sizes are set from heuristic upper estimates of the best known attack (o(1) dropped, calibrated constants); neither MSS nor BD nor any read source gives a lower bound on finite-field DLP cost, and BD state that a security estimation would ideally require one.
nodes.scope: Applies to every 'bits of security' figure for a pairing target field and to every transfer-audit price of F_(q^k).
source_locations: Barbulescu-Duquesne 2019, Section 4.3.1 (upper bound vs lower bound remark)

nodes.label: Sparse medium subfield representation
nodes.statement: F_{q^2k} is represented as F_{q^2}[X]/(I) with I an irreducible degree-k factor of h1(X) X^q - h0(X), deg h0, deg h1 <= delta for a constant delta (2 in practice), so that X^q = h0/h1 modulo I.
nodes.scope: The field model behind BGJT and the GKZ descent; KW replace it by an elliptic-curve model that provably exists.

nodes.label: BGJT heuristic: a sparse medium subfield representation exists
nodes.statement: Every field F_{q^2k} with k <= q + 2 admits a sparse medium subfield representation with deg h0, deg h1 <= 2 (and small-characteristic fields embed into such a field of slightly larger size).
nodes.scope: Heuristically almost certain; attempts to prove existence have failed (Micheli 2019, cited by KW).
source_locations: BGJT 2014, Section 2 and Section 1 (first of 'three key heuristics')

nodes.label: BGJT descent heuristics (smoothness and PGL2 full rank)
nodes.statement: Heuristic 7: for any P(X), the rows v(m) for cosets m in PGL2(F_{q^2})/PGL2(F_q) that yield a relation have full rank q^2 + 1; Heuristic 8: the linear system for P = X has full rank; plus smoothness of the non-uniform polynomials arising matches that of random polynomials of the same degree.
nodes.scope: Needed for Proposition 2 (each node of the descent costs poly(q,k)); fails as literally stated for problematic polynomials dividing h1 X^q - h0 (traps), which BGJT v2 Proposition 10 and CWZ patch with further heuristics.

nodes.label: BGJT heuristic quasi-polynomial DLP in small characteristic
nodes.statement: Assuming the representation and descent heuristics, any discrete logarithm in F_{q^2k} is computed in max(q,k)^O(log k) (Theorem 3); for q ~ k this is 2^O((log log Q)^2) (Corollary 4); for characteristic bounded by (log Q)^O(1) it is 2^O((log log Q)^2) (Corollary 5), e.g. F_{2^n} in 2^O((log n)^2); for q <= L_Q(alpha) it is L_Q(alpha)^O(log log Q) (Corollary 6).
nodes.scope: Heuristic; constant in the exponent unspecified. The first quasi-polynomial claim, later made rigorous (GKZ for infinitely many n; KW for all n).
assumptions: BGJT representation heuristic
BGJT descent heuristics, as patched for traps

cited_by.note: Prices the ECC2K-130 MOV target with N^O(log N), past 2^900.

nodes.label: Claim: BGJT descent step applies to every polynomial P
nodes.statement: Proposition 2 part 1 (each P of degree 2..k-1 rewrites as O(kq^2) logarithms of polynomials of degree <= ceil(deg P / 2)) holds for every P under Heuristic 7, and part 2 yields the logarithms of all linear X + a.
nodes.scope: Refuted as stated for 'problematic' polynomials: irreducible factors of h1 X^q - h0 other than the defining one (traps), and linear factors in the non-Kummer case. BGJT v2 itself concedes it and adds Proposition 10; CWZ give an alternative fix. The quasi-polynomial claim survives only through these patched, still heuristic, steps.
assumptions: As printed in the original BGJT heuristic analysis
source_locations: BGJT 2014 (arXiv v2), Section 5 'An obstruction to the heuristics'

nodes.label: Cheng-Wan-Zhuang traps in the BGJT descent
nodes.statement: The computation really takes place in F_{q^2}[x]/(x^q h1 - h0), not modulo the minimal polynomial; if W(x) divides x^q h1(x) - h0(x) then the coefficient e1 in the descent relation is always 0 (Theorem 3), so such W cannot be descended by the original method; when x^q h1 - h0 has linear factors the factor-base step can fail too.
nodes.scope: Exact statements about the BGJT relation construction; the proposed fix (Heuristics 1-3, Proposition 1) is itself heuristic.
assumptions: deg h1 <= 2 for the structural theorems

nodes.label: GKZ: rigorous quasi-polynomial DLP for infinitely many F_{p^n}
nodes.statement: Theorem 1: for every prime p there are infinitely many explicit extensions F_{p^n} with DLP solvable in expected time exp((1/log 2 + o(1))(log n)^2). Theorem 2: for a prime power q > 61 not a power of 4, k >= 18, coprime h0, h1 in F_{q^k}[X] of degree <= 2 and an irreducible degree-l factor I of h1 X^q - h0, the DLP in F_{q^{kl}} = F_{q^k}[X]/(I) is solved in expected time q^(log2 l + O(k)).
nodes.scope: Rigorous (randomized) and free of smoothness heuristics, but only for fields with such a representation (e.g. Kummer case l = q - 1).
assumptions: Existence of the representation (h0,h1,I) with the stated parameters
source_locations: GKZ 2018, Theorem 1 and Theorem 2 (Section 1); Theorem 3 proved in Section 4
nodes.formula: exp((1/log 2 + o(1))(log n)^2); q^(log2 l + O(k))

nodes.label: GKZ representation conjecture (all extensions)
nodes.statement: For p fixed and every n there exist q = p^i >= n - 2 (not too large) and 18 <= k = o(log q) with h0, h1 in F_{q^k}[X] of degree <= 2 such that h1 X^q - h0 has an irreducible factor of degree n.
nodes.scope: GKZ call proving it 'a very hard problem, even if heuristically it would appear to be almost certain'; Kleinjung-Wesolowski bypass it with an elliptic-curve model.
source_locations: GKZ 2018, Section 1 (paragraph after Theorem 2) and abstract

nodes.label: GKZ conditional: quasi-polynomial DLP in every F_{p^n}
nodes.statement: Subject to the representation conjecture, the GKZ algorithm solves the DLP in every F_{p^n} (p fixed) in expected time exp((1/log 2 + o(1))(log n)^2).
nodes.scope: Superseded as a route to an unconditional statement by Kleinjung-Wesolowski 2019.
assumptions: GKZ representation conjecture

nodes.label: KW: elliptic-curve models of F_{p^{rn}} exist and are constructible
nodes.statement: For any prime p and integer n one can find, in deterministic time polynomial in p and n, r = O(log n) and a (p^r, n)-elliptic curve model (E, Q, I) of F_{p^{rn}}: an ordinary E/F_q with a rational point Q of order n and a degree-n place I with f o phi_q = f o tau_Q mod I.
nodes.scope: Replaces the unproved sparse-subfield representation (Frobenius acts as translation by Q on the place I).

nodes.label: Kleinjung-Wesolowski: proved quasi-polynomial DLP in fixed characteristic
nodes.statement: For any prime p and positive integer n, the DLP in F_{p^n}^* can be solved in expected time (pn)^(2 log2 n + O(1)); for fixed p this is n^(2 log2 n + O(1)), quasi-polynomial; for p = L_{p^n}(alpha), alpha in (0, 1/2), it gives L_{p^n}(alpha + o(1)).
nodes.scope: Rigorous, randomized (expected time). Small and fixed characteristic; says nothing about large-characteristic or medium-prime fields where NFS variants are heuristic.
source_locations: Kleinjung-Wesolowski 2019, Theorem 1.1 (proof completed in Section 7.1 from Theorem 3.1)
non_implications: Quasi-polynomial in n is not practical at astronomically large n: targets of size ~r bits (ordinary curves) stay infeasible

cited_by.note: States quasi-polynomial small-characteristic algorithms are not modeled in the pairing prices.

nodes.label: No proved L(1/3) DLP in large or medium characteristic
nodes.statement: In the sources read, every L(1/3) complexity for F_p or medium-prime F_{p^n} (NFS, TNFS, exTNFS, SNFS) is heuristic, while the proved bounds there remain L(1/2); only fixed (and L(alpha < 1/2)) characteristic has proved sub-L(1/2) results (KW).
nodes.scope: Every pairing transfer to a large- or medium-characteristic target field (BN, BLS, KSS, MNT; supersingular over F_p with k = 2) therefore inherits heuristic, not proved, target costs.
source_locations: Kim-Barbulescu 2016, Thm. 1 ('under the classical NFS heuristics')

nodes.label: Rigorous quasi-polynomial ECDLP on supersingular curves of fixed characteristic
nodes.statement: For supersingular E over F_{p^m} with p fixed (e.g. 2 or 3) and prime r | #E with embedding degree k <= 6, the MOV/Frey-Rueck pairing maps the ECDLP in polynomial time into F_{p^{mk}}^*, where Kleinjung-Wesolowski solve it in expected time (p mk)^(2 log2(mk) + O(1)); hence the ECDLP on such curves is quasi-polynomial in m without heuristics.
nodes.scope: Composition assembled in this corpus from proved pieces; no read source states it in this form, so it is kept conditional until the composition (pairing evaluation, nondegeneracy sampling, subgroup bookkeeping) is written out and reviewed.
assumptions: E supersingular, k <= 6 (THEOREM-SUPERSINGULAR-SMALL-K)
Pairing nondegenerate on the target subgroup and computable by Miller's algorithm in poly(m) time
Reduction from F_{q^k} subgroup DLP to full F_{q^k}^* DLP via KW

nodes.label: Claim: Joux pinpointing reaches L(1/3, (8/9)^(1/3))
nodes.statement: Joux's December 2012 'pinpointing' relation method for medium base fields has heuristic complexity L(1/3, (8/9)^(1/3)) ~ L(1/3, 0.961).
nodes.scope: The constant as originally printed; corrected after later communications.
nodes.notes: Known only through the GKZ footnote ('The original paper states a complexity of L(1/3,(8/9)^(1/3)) ... on foot of recent communications the constant should be as stated'). The Joux paper itself was not read.

nodes.label: Joux pinpointing: corrected constant L(1/3, 2^(1/3))
nodes.statement: For medium-sized base fields the pinpointing technique has heuristic complexity as low as L(1/3, 2^(1/3)) ~ L(1/3, 1.260), improving on Joux-Lercier's L(1/3, 3^(1/3)).
nodes.scope: Heuristic; a corrected constant reported by GKZ.
assumptions: FFS-type smoothness heuristics

nodes.label: Total break of the DLP in F_{2^{12*367}} (genus-2 supersingular pairing target)
nodes.statement: The DLP in F_{2^{12*367}}, the embedding field (k = 12) of a supersingular genus-two curve over F_{2^367} proposed at the '128-bit' level, was solved in about 52240 core-hours (2^48 M_r2); the paper prints the resulting logarithm.
nodes.scope: A completed record computation (its output logarithm can be checked), using only L(1/4)-type techniques; no BGJT quasi-polynomial elimination was needed.
assumptions: Correct implementation; the printed logarithm verifies
source_locations: GKZ 2014, Section 5.4 'Summary' and Section 1 contribution list

nodes.label: Claim: the genus-2 supersingular curve over F_{2^367} gives 128-bit security
nodes.statement: The pairing on the Jacobian of a supersingular genus-two curve over F_{2^367} with embedding degree 12 offers 128-bit security (target field F_{2^{12*367}} sized with Coppersmith-era estimates).
nodes.scope: Refuted by a completed computation of a discrete logarithm in the target field.
assumptions: Target field priced with pre-2013 small-characteristic algorithms
source_locations: GKZ 2014, Section 1 (Adj et al. upper bound 2^94.6; originally '128-bit secure')

nodes.label: GKZ: the genus-1 supersingular F_{2^1223} target has about 59-bit security
nodes.statement: The DLP in F_{2^{4*1223}} (embedding field of the commonly implemented supersingular genus-one curve over F_{2^1223}, k = 4, r a 1221-bit prime) can be solved in approximately 2^40 s, or 2^59 M_r.
nodes.scope: A step-by-step costed estimate, not a completed computation; relies on descent success heuristics at each stage.
assumptions: Descent and elimination steps succeed as in the cost analysis (heuristic)
source_locations: GKZ 2014, Section 1 contribution list and Section 4

nodes.label: Claim: new small-characteristic algorithms leave the F_{2^1223} genus-1 curve at ~128 bits
nodes.statement: Adj, Menezes, Oliveira and Rodriguez-Henriquez suggested that the 2013 algorithms have no impact on the security of the supersingular genus-one curve over F_{2^1223} (k = 4), which stays very close to 128 bits.
nodes.scope: Refuted within the concrete-estimate model by GKZ's costed descent (~2^59 M_r); not by a completed computation.
source_locations: GKZ 2014, Section 1 (summary of Adj et al.) and Section 6 Conclusion
nodes.notes: The Adj et al. paper itself was not read; its claim is as summarized by GKZ.

edges.statement: Xedni is the global-nontorsion 'easy lifting' instance of the lifting problem: curve and up to 9 points lifted simultaneously by linear algebra.
Lifted index calculus is the global-nontorsion 'hard lifting' face with a factor base of small-height points.
Few small-height points in E~(Q) force exponentially large lifts of random points (heuristic).
Silverman-Suzuki develop Miller's brief heuristic into a detailed analysis.
The natural lifted index calculus is estimated to be slower than brute force.
A working growing-factor-base lift would construct curves over Q of arbitrarily large rank.
The bounded-rank obstruction is HKT's implication read contrapositively.
The obstruction needs ranks over Q to be bounded, which is only heuristic.
Under bounded rank, no lift of a growing number of random points to bounded height exists.
Classic xedni lifts a fixed number (<= 9) of points; HKT's hypothesis is an asymptotically increasing number.
Cheng-Huang split the HKT lifting obstacle into three partial lifting problems under rank heuristics.
An algorithm for the three partial lifting problems solves ECDLP, assuming the rank heuristics.
Local nontorsion lifts lose T = mS unless each Hensel step is chosen consistently, which needs m.
Torsion lifts keep the relation but give O = mO in the formal group.
Torsion over Q is at most 16; number fields carrying order-n torsion have degree ~n^4.
The lift of T has height m^2 h(S): O(p^2) bits and no known way to find it.
Explains why the p-adic/formal-group attack works only for l = p and gives no leak for l != p.
Same structure: l-torsion (l != p) lifts isomorphically through E(Z/p^2).
Torsion over number fields is polynomially bounded in degree and Szpiro ratio, quantifying how large K must be.
The < 1/p dependence heuristic is extrapolated from Masser's density-zero theorem.
Simultaneously lifted points are almost never dependent, so xedni rarely yields a relation.
Independent route (Masser specialization) to the same order-1/p per-trial success as JKSST's height-based C0/p bound.
Quadratic growth of h gives no uniform lower-bound constant; the JKSST Lean audit has an explicit scaled-lattice countermodel.
JKSST's C0/p bound assumes Lang's conjecture (or a direct uniform height gap) for the selected lifts.
Lang follows from Szpiro's conjecture.
Szpiro (bounded sigma) is a sufficient condition for Lang via Hindry-Silverman/Petsche.
Replaces the Lang hypothesis by an unconditional explicit constant c(d, sigma), provided the Szpiro ratio of the selected lifts is bounded.
Turns the 'Lang or direct height gap' bridge into the measurable question of the Szpiro ratio of selected lifts.
Polynomial-time when the subgroup order is the characteristic (anomalous case).
Semaev's differential method and Smart's p-adic lift solve the same anomalous case.
Independent p-adic (Fermat-quotient) formulation of the anomalous attack.
The elliptic anomalous attack is the genus-one case of Rueck's p-torsion method.
The anomalous exclusion in curve screens is justified by this polynomial-time attack.
The Weil-pairing MOV attack can be run in E(F_{q^k}) with k the embedding degree when r does not divide q-1.
The bound is on the probability of small embedding degree.
For random prime-order curves the MOV/FR transfer is subexponential only with negligible probability.
The embedding-degree screen rejects a rare event for random curves; it matters for constructed/special curves.
On ECC2K-130 the transfer target exceeds 1.3e9 bits, so MOV/FR is not a route there.
Low-embedding-degree ordinary curves are scarce and must be constructed; they are not found by random search.
The theorem asserts existence of distortion maps.

With a distortion map the pairing is nondegenerate on

x

, so DDH in

becomes easy on supersingular curves.
Supersingular curves with a distortion map realize Type 1 pairings.
The trace is not a distortion map for the Frobenius eigenspaces G1, G2, consistent with Type 3 settings lacking an efficient homomorphism.
Which source-group problems a pairing exposes depends on its type.
Complexities are stated in L notation.
NFS L(1/3) complexities are derived from the smoothness heuristic.
Kim-Barbulescu Theorem 1 holds 'under the classical NFS heuristics'.
The 2^99.69 estimate uses Dickman smoothness of Monte Carlo norm sizes.
All recommended sizes come from the same heuristic cost model.
MSS estimates also rest on the NFS smoothness heuristics.
Coppersmith's L(1/3) bound rests on polynomial smoothness heuristics for the non-uniform values sieved.
The BN estimate uses SexTNFS, the special-p variant of exTNFS.
Key sizes assume the attacker uses (S)exTNFS where it applies.
An explicit SexTNFS parameterization costs about 2^99.7 < 2^128 in the same heuristic cost model the claim used.
BD show the MSS norm upper bounds sit far above 99.9% of sampled norms and that MSS omit filtering; both give attack upper estimates, not security lower bounds.
Key sizes are upper estimates of the best known attack, not lower bounds on cost.
The target-field cost that governs a pairing attack has no proved lower bound; only best-known-attack estimates.
c = 32 is argued (not proved) to be the floor of the NFS family in large/medium characteristic.
Heuristic L(1/3) upper bound on the target-field DLP for prime and general fields.
Heuristic L(1/3,(48/9)^(1/3)) / (32/9)^(1/3) for the composite-n medium-prime targets of BN/BLS pairings.
Historic heuristic bound for binary targets.
Proved L(1/2) bound in any characteristic covered (prime fields; fixed characteristic per Pomerance).
Heuristic quasi-polynomial bound for small-characteristic targets.
Proved expected quasi-polynomial bound for fixed-characteristic targets.
The L(1/3) complexities remain unproved.
exTNFS complexities remain unproved.
The heuristic asserts that such a representation exists.
First of BGJT's three key heuristics.
Proposition 2, hence Theorem 3, rests on Heuristics 7 and 8 and smoothness of non-uniform polynomials.
Factors of x^q h1 - h0 (traps) get e1 = 0 and cannot be descended; BGJT v2 concedes Proposition 2 cannot hold for them.
The descent heuristics as originally stated are problematic in the non-Kummer case; patched versions are still heuristic.
The quasi-polynomial claim must route around the refuted universal step (Proposition 10 or the CWZ fix).
GKZ Theorem 2 is stated for fields given in this representation (degree <= 2 h0, h1).
GKZ's descent removes the smoothness heuristics, proving quasi-polynomial time where the representation exists.
The all-n statement needs the representation conjecture.
Theorem 2 is applied after embedding F_{p^n} into a suitable F_{q^{kn}}.
The provably existing elliptic-curve model replaces the conjectural representation.

research_targets.label: Replace Lang by a measured Szpiro-ratio bound for xedni lifts
research_targets.objective: Decide whether the Lang hypothesis in the JKSST obstruction can be replaced by Petsche's unconditional c(d, sigma) bound: measure the Szpiro ratio of the curves the xedni/JKSST lift selection actually produces, and prove or refute a uniform bound for that family.
research_targets.acceptance: Either a proof that sigma is bounded on the selected-lift family (then the obstruction's Lang bridge becomes unconditional with an explicit constant), or a measured family where sigma grows, recorded with exact discriminants and conductors.
research_targets.next_step: Generate lifts with the repository's frozen xedni lift procedure for p up to 2^20, compute minimal discriminant and conductor (PARI/Sage), and tabulate sigma against p.

research_targets.label: Correct the transfer audit's 'lower bound' for F_(q^k) prices
research_targets.objective: The transfer audit prices F_(q^k) DLP by L[1/3, (32/9)^(1/3)] with o(1) dropped and calls it an attacker-favourable lower bound. research_targets.label: Prove the rigorous quasi-polynomial ECDLP on supersingular small-characteristic curves
research_targets.objective: Write out (and ideally formalize the bookkeeping of) the composition MOV/Frey-Rueck + Kleinjung-Wesolowski, so COND-XT-MOV-SS-SMALLCHAR becomes a reviewed theorem: pairing evaluation cost, nondegenerate partner-point sampling, subgroup-to-field DLP reduction, and the final expected-time bound in terms of m.
research_targets.acceptance: A written proof with every step's cost and probability, reviewed, giving expected time (p m k)^(2 log2(mk)+O(1)) times poly(m) for k <= 6.
research_targets.next_step: Draft the proof in papers/, citing KW Theorem 1.1 and Galbraith Theorem 26.4.1/26.4.2, and check the r | q - 1 edge case separately.
